desc: Parse N, M, A, B and the M bad intervals (sorted, disjoint).
Precompute the set of representable numbers (non-negative integers reachable as sum of allowed step sizes A..B) up to bound = A*B + A.
Process each good interval: start at S=1, for each bad [L,R] the good interval is [S, L-1]; define target window T = [R+1-B, R+1-A]; check T ∩ [S, L-1] is non-empty; if empty -> No.
For the intersection [K1, K2] (offsets from S), check if any representable number lies in [K1, K2]; if not -> No. Otherwise update S = R+1 and continue.
After processing all bad intervals, at final S = R_M+1, check if N - S is representable; print Yes/No accordingly.
Test on the provided samples (24 2 3 5 -> Yes; 30 1 5 8 -> No; 100 4 10 11 -> Yes).
Review the previous DSU-based approach and determine it is overcomplicated; switch to the simpler representable-numbers greedy method.
